title: Building Near Airports Could Get Easier As Centre Plans Automated, Time-Bound NOC System
text:
Infrastructure
Swarajya Staff
Sep 03, 2026 | Updated 09:47 AM GMT+5:30

Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu has directed senior officials to work out modalities for simplifying, automating and decentralising the aviation No Objection Certificate (NOC) process within 15 days.
The minister emphasised the need to make the issuance of NOCs hassle-free, transparent, automated and time-bound, with minimal manual intervention during a meeting with Ministry of Civil Aviation and Airports Authority of India officials on Wednesday.
The proposed reforms aim to facilitate members of the general public, societies, builders and industry whilst ensuring regulatory requirements related to aviation safety continue to be addressed.
The meeting was organised to review measures for promoting Ease of Doing Business in the civil aviation sector, with particular emphasis on streamlining the NOC issuance process.
The minister discussed the feasibility of providing permissible building heights to applicants at the initial stage itself, particularly in major metropolitan cities such as Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
Such an approach would enable applicants and stakeholders to take informed decisions and plan their building development in accordance with applicable height restrictions from the outset.
The existing geographical coverage of the No Objection Certificate Application System currently covers areas within 20 kilometres for Visual Flight Rules operations and 56 kilometres for Instrument Flight Rules operations.
Officials examined whether NOCs can be issued at the Urban Local Body level wherever feasible, reducing the need for individuals and industries to approach AAI directly.
The overall objective of these reforms is to ensure expeditious and time-bound clearance of proposals, with relevant data and permissible height information made transparently available in the public domain, including through websites, without compromising aviation safety.
The ministry is also considering changes to the Aeronautical Study process, including reducing the requirement for physical verification of sites at the initial stage.
